terrain: floating islands in two stacked layers, flat-topped plateaus
changed: The single continuous landmass became separate skyland plateaus with open sky between them and a second, smaller layer of islands above. The 14 biomes now come in regions over the land instead of narrow bands.
why: Open sky covers 42% of the map and islands stand over islands in 10% of columns. The ground is mostly level tops, and 11 of the 12 surface biomes show their own plants and trees. Wisteria is still only 4.6% of the map, and grove regions are small for a meeting of a few places: the largest three hold 31% of the land.
ownersEye: The boundary between the cherry and meadow regions runs almost straight north to south across several islands. Is that acceptable?
Should the flat island tops be flatter or more rolling?

terrain: vanilla overworld on its own seed, stretched 1.67 times, 65% land
changed: Land share set to 65%. A larger climate scale was tried and rejected because it made the world colder.
why: The world has ordinary forests, plains and seas, with water on 37% of it. On this seed it is cold, though: snow or ice covers 28%, and snowy taiga is the largest biome at 16%. The biomes form a scatter, with the largest three land regions holding only 10% of the land.
exception: Broad regions need the climate stretched 3 to 4 times. On this seed that spreads the cold to 37% and 47% snow cover. A seed with temperate land near spawn, or a per-dimension temperature shift, would close it.

terrain: vanilla Nether cavern, biome regions stretched 2.5 times
changed: The base Nether now lists the five vanilla biomes plus quartz flats, laid out as large regions with the crimson forest weighted highest.
why: Crimson forest is the largest biome at 30% and warped forest covers 22%. Lava covers 17% and the roof covers 94% of the map. The largest three regions hold 61% of the land, but the land splits into ten major regions rather than eight.
ownersEye: Should quartz flats, the white Nether, be part of the base Nether?

terrain: vanilla End on its own seed
changed: No generator change. Re-surveyed with the current survey.
why: Void covers 47% of the map. End midlands and highlands lead, and all four biomes show. The largest island covers 176 hectares. Chorus is thin at 0.7% of top blocks, and the cities near the gateways were not measured.

terrain: one floating island gathered at spawn, void beyond
changed: The island field copied from the Aviary became one snowy island about 800 blocks across, with fir forest, snowy plains, slopes and a dying forest for the autumnal tundra.
why: There is one island of 57 hectares in open void, and snow lies on 79% of its ground. All six listed biomes show. The 1.21.1 frozen cliffs are gone, and the island splits into five biome regions rather than reading as one fir forest.
ownersEye: Is an island about 800 blocks across big enough for 'animal country'?

terrain: a ring of plateau islands with drowned basins
changed: The copied island field became a ring of plateau islands 300 blocks out, with deep water basins in it held by the deep oceans. The deep dark surface and the gold grove are gone.
why: The basins are deep, with 83% of the water more than 12 blocks deep, and all five listed biomes show. The middle of the ring is void, not water, and water covers only 19% of the ground.
exception: There is no single drowned hollow at the centre. The basin terrain lays many small basins, and one big central lake drowned 76% of the ground. A basin terrain whose single lake is the layout's hollow would close it.
ownersEye: The noon shots do not look as dark as the shrine's dark-blue sky asks. Should it be darker?

terrain: stone spires rising 120 blocks from islets of their own, faced with amethyst
changed: The copied island field became spires on islets, with lavender and wisteria leading, amethyst on the spire faces, purpur on the chorus forest, and both crystal and jungle patches kept.
why: Lavender (15%) and wisteria (11%) lead. Amethyst is 3.8% of top blocks, and spires reach y 239. The land is 82 islets of at most 5 hectares, so it reads as a scatter: 51% of the land lies in specks.
exception: Each spire stands on its own islet. Stacked floating islands in their place lost the spires. Spires that can stand on shared floating islands would close it.
ownersEye: Spires on islets, or wide violet islands without spires: which reads closer to 'violet spires in the sky'?

terrain: sky islands joined into large drowned basins, with a second layer of islands above
changed: The copied island field became island masses holding warm water in their basins, with the ocean biomes in the water, jungle and highlands on the islands, and a layer of smaller islands above.
why: Water covers 45% of the map and void only 13%. The warm oceans lie in the basins, jungle covers 21% and highlands 16%, and islands sit above in 19% of columns. Islets inside the basins break the land into small regions: the largest three hold 14% of it.
